artworks.title: Apollo and Daphne (marble, Galleria Borghese, Rome)
artworks.description: Bernini's Baroque marble catches Ovid's instant of change — bark closing over Daphne's flesh as Apollo's hand still grasps what is already becoming laurel. The Thessalian nymph of Peneus, not the Arcadian huntress of the Ladon, is the figure the poets crown with Apollo's tree.

music.title: Dafne
music.description: Peri's Dafne is often called the first opera — Daphne's flight from Apollo as the newborn art form's founding subject.

popCulture.title: Apollo and Daphne
popCulture.creator: Gian Lorenzo Bernini
popCulture.description: Bernini's marble in the Galleria Borghese freezes the metamorphosis mid-stride — bark racing up Daphne's body as Apollo reaches.

popCulture.title: Daphne
popCulture.description: Daphne endures as the laurel of poetry itself — the nymph who became the crown Apollo still wears.
